title: Recommendations (How YouTube Works)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date). Recommendations on Home and Up Next use viewing behaviour, likes, dislikes, subscriptions and satisfaction-survey feedback, plus channel reputation and quality and outside evaluators; viewers can pause or delete watch and search history

title: How YouTube search works
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). The old How YouTube Works search page redirects here. Search ranks on relevance (title, tags, description, video content, watch time for the query), engagement and quality (expertise, authoritativeness, trustworthiness); results are personalised; YouTube takes no payment for better organic placement

title: Add tags to your videos
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Title, thumbnail and description matter more than tags for discovery; tags play a minimal role except for commonly misspelled subjects; excessive tags in a description break the spam policy

title: Get started with YouTube Analytics
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Analytics tabs Overview, Content, Reach, Engagement, Audience, Revenue (YPP only) and Trends; Reach shows impressions, CTR, views, unique viewers; Engagement shows watch time, average view duration and Engaged views; Audience shows new, casual and regular viewers; updated YouTube Studio rolling out gradually from July 2026

title: Trends tab in YouTube Analytics
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Trends tab shows top searches from your audience and saved searches over 28 days, breakout videos from similar creators, recent videos and content gaps for Shorts; some insights limited by country, language and device; saving searches

title: Impressions and click-through rate
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Impressions CTR definition; half of all channels and videos range between 2% and 10%, wider for new channels and videos under 100 views; lower CTR for widely shown videos; external sites and end screens excluded; high CTR with low average view duration and lower impressions can signal clickbait

title: Measure key moments for audience retention
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Audience retention report reading (flat, gradual decline, spikes, dips); typical retention uses your 10 latest videos of similar length; Intro = share still watching after 30 seconds; key moments need videos of 60 seconds or more with at least 100 views

title: Understand your YouTube video reach
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Definitions of traffic sources: Browse features, Channel pages, End screens, Shorts, Notifications, Playlists, Suggested videos, YouTube search, External, Direct or unknown and others

title: Add video thumbnails on YouTube
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Custom thumbnails need a verified account; recommended 3840 x 2160 at 16:9, minimum width 640; Shorts 2160 x 3840 at 9:16; JPG or PNG; 2 MB on mobile, 50 MB on desktop; vertical videos with 16:9 thumbnails get an automatic 4:5 thumbnail on some surfaces; daily thumbnail limits

title: Test & compare thumbnails and titles
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Up to 3 titles, thumbnails or both; desktop YouTube Studio; winner chosen by watch time share with a control group; results Winner, Performed Same, Inconclusive; tests finish within about two weeks; not for Shorts, made-for-kids, mature or private videos; thumbnails below 1280 x 720 cause downscaling

title: Thumbnails policy
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Thumbnails that are sexual, violent, gory, vulgar or that mislead viewers about the video are not allowed; removal, warnings, strikes and termination

title: Video chapters
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Chapters in the description; first timestamp 00:00; at least three timestamps in ascending order; each at least 10 seconds; manual chapters override automatic chapters

title: Add end screens to videos
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Video at least 25 seconds; end screens in the last 5 to 20 seconds; up to four elements on 16:9; link element needs YouTube Partner Program; not available on made-for-kids videos

title: Understand three-minute YouTube Shorts
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Square or vertical videos up to three minutes uploaded on or after 15 October 2024 are Shorts; a Short over one minute with an active copyright claim is blocked globally and cannot be recommended or monetised; most Shorts Audio Library songs usable for up to 90 seconds

title: YouTube Partner Program overview & eligibility
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). 1,000 subscribers plus 4,000 qualified watch hours in 12 months or 10 million qualified Shorts views in 90 days; 2-Step Verification, AdSense for YouTube, no active strikes; updated YPP terms take effect 1 February 2027, to be accepted by 31 January 2027

title: YouTube channel monetization policies
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). On 15 July 2025 the repetitious content policy was renamed inauthentic content (mass-produced, templated, barely varied, including generic AI templates); reused content rules and examples

title: Spam policy
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Malicious clickbait (titles, thumbnails, descriptions that do not deliver), engagement manipulation such as sub-for-sub and bots or rewards, fake engagement with polls, comment spam

title: Community Guidelines strike basics on YouTube
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Warning first with optional policy training; first strike one week, second two weeks, third within 90 days may end the channel; strikes last 90 days; deleting content does not remove a strike

title: Determining if your content is made for kids
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Every creator must set whether content is made for kids, under an agreement with the FTC and COPPA; factors; mixed-audience content counts; creators are legally responsible; under 13 in the US

title: Paid product placements and endorsements
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Paid Promotion setting in YouTube Studio ("Yes, my video includes branded content"); disclosure label at the start of the video; creators and partners must follow local law, naming the FTC and ASA among others

title: Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). What realistic AI content must be disclosed and what need not be; AI use setting in Attributes; labels in player or description; disclosure does not limit reach or earnings; consistent non-disclosure can lead to added labels, removal or YPP suspension

title: Manage channel permissions
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Roles Owner, Manager, Editor, Editor (Limited), Subtitle Editor, Viewer, Viewer (Limited) and what each can do; limited roles cannot see revenue; invitations expire after 30 days

title: Video SEO best practices
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Watch pages, VideoObject structured data, video sitemaps, thumbnails; key moments via Clip and SeekToAction markup or YouTube chapters, which Google prioritises

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Guides revised 2023; on YouTube a description-only disclosure is not enough; disclose in the video, at the start or before the endorsement, spoken and shown; disclose affiliate links in the video and near the links

title: Recognising ads: Social media and influencer marketing
supports: Opened with WebFetch; dated 6 Aug 2026. Labels such as Ad; vague labels insufficient; on YouTube an identifier such as Ad in the title and/or thumbnail; brand and influencer both responsible

title: Influencer Legal Hub
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date; legal briefs dated 11 Oct 2023). EU consumer law requires brand partnerships and affiliate marketing to be disclosed; cites a 2018 Princeton study finding 10% of affiliate marketing on YouTube and Pinterest disclosed

title: AI Act (regulatory framework for AI)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 19 Oct 2026. Transparency rules, including clear labels on deepfakes, apply from August 2026; code of practice on marking and labelling AI content; transparency guidelines (July 2026)

title: CSGO Lotto owners settle FTC's first-ever complaint against individual social media influencers
supports: Opened with WebFetch; 7 Sep 2017. YouTube creators promoted a site they owned without saying so; other creators paid $2,500 to $55,000; settlement requires clear disclosure of material connections

title: Google and YouTube will pay record $170 million for alleged violations of children's privacy law
supports: Opened with WebFetch; 4 Sep 2019. $170 million ($136 million FTC, $34 million New York); settlement requires a system for channel owners to identify child-directed content and notices that it may be subject to COPPA

title: YouTube SEO: How to rank your videos from start to finish (Sam Oh)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last updated 28 May 2020, describing 2019 results. One video a week on searched topics; over 3 million minutes of watch time in about seven months; one video 28,700 views and over 1,400 subscribers in two weeks; a series not built on searched topics drew little search traffic. The company's own account
